										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Argentina&#8217;s tax authority (ARCA) <a href="https://servicioscf.afip.gob.ar/publico/sitio/contenido/novedad/ver.aspx?id=5828" target="_blank" rel="noopener">announced</a> on 29 July 2026 that it has scrapped value limits on postal and courier exports under General Resolution ARCA No. 5883, effective 30 July 2026, and has streamlined documentation requirements for incoming small shipments.</p>
<p>The regulation cuts red tape on two fronts. Exporters can now send goods abroad via courier without hitting a ceiling on value. For importers buying small parcels, the bureaucracy shrinks: you no longer declare tariff positions for duty-free, fee-free purchases—just provide your AFIP/ARCA code.</p>
<p><strong>What the new thresholds are</strong></p>
<p>Small shipments stay capped at USD 3,000 per parcel, 50 kg per package, with a five-shipment annual limit per person. These are exempt from food and cosmetics controls, technical standards, and licenses or antidumping checks.</p>
<p>Commercial samples, available only to legal entities, hit the same USD 3,000 and 50 kg ceiling, but get a special carve-out if customs value doesn&#8217;t exceed USD 100.</p>
<p>The regulations take effect on 30 July 2026. Their provisions will be implemented according to the schedule published on the <a href="https://www.arca.gob.ar/envios-internacionales/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">“International Shipments” microsite</a>.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>The Philippines has introduced a new package of tax incentives for the electric vehicle sector under the Electric Vehicle Incentive Strategy (EVIS) Programme, approved through <a href="https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/2026/07/29/executive-order-no-121-s-2026/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Executive Order No. 121</a>.</p>
<p>Executive Order No. 121 establishes the EVIS Programme in the Philippines pursuant to Republic Act No. 11697 (the Electric Vehicle Industry Development Act or EVIDA).</p>
<p>Approved by the Fiscal Incentives Review Board (FIRB) under Resolution No. 009-26 on 18 May 2026 and signed on 29 July 2026, the programme is designed to narrow the cost gap between electric vehicles (EVs) and traditional vehicles, shift local manufacturing toward electric mobility, and position the Philippines as a regional automotive manufacturing hub.</p>
<p>Qualified manufacturers can receive Fixed Investment Support covering up to 40% of capital costs and Production Volume Incentives for every unit assembled domestically. To ensure accountability, the order creates an Inter-Agency Committee to oversee registration, monitor performance standards, and audit the participants&#8217; compliance with sustainability goals.</p>
<p>The key measures are as follows:</p>
<p><strong>Coverage</strong></p>
<p>The EVIS programme targets both hybrid vehicles (HEVs, PHEVs, FCEVs) and battery EVs (BEVs), covering passenger and commercial segments plus their parts and components.</p>
<p><strong>Fiscal support package</strong></p>
<p>Money moves through two channels. Fixed Investment Support (FIS) covers capex on tooling, R&amp;D, engineering, start-up costs, and training, for up to 10 years from model registration. BEVs get 40%, hybrids get 30%. Production Volume Incentive (PVI) pays up to 12% of the ex-factory price per unit, capped at PhP 200,000, running for up to 10 years from the start of production.</p>
<p><strong>Eligibility and technical requirements</strong></p>
<p>To qualify for FIS, a company needs PHP 5 billion in new investment and has to bring the enrolled model to market within three years of registration.</p>
<p>PVI requires actual local assembly of the mandatory components and a production plan of at least 10,000 units. Each participant can enrol a maximum of two EV models. If more companies apply than the programme can support, the Board of Investments (BOI) will select the top four based on economic impact. Everyone enrolled also needs to meet UNR 100 and/or UNR 136 standards, plus commit to battery recycling and 10 years of spare parts support.</p>
<p><strong>Funding cap and tax payment certificates</strong></p>
<p>The whole programme is capped at PHP 60 billion, funded through the National Expenditure Programme (NEP) and General Appropriations Act, with no single model allowed to draw more than PHP 15 billion. Instead of cash, companies get Tax Payment Certificates (TPCs) they can use against income tax, excise tax, VAT, or import duties. These certificates aren&#8217;t transferable.</p>
<p><strong>Governance and restrictions</strong></p>
<p>BOI runs the show as lead agency, backed by the IAC-EV committee (DOF, DOE, DOTr, DBM). Companies can&#8217;t double-dip between EVIS and Title XIII incentives under the Tax Code. BOI also audits participants to catch parts trading, and anyone who misses their investment or three-year deadline faces refunds, forfeiture, fines, or gets bounced from the programme entirely.</p>
<p>The EVIS programme is effective from 30 July 2026.</p>

<p>ARCA moved from manual inspection at arrival to advance digital validation. Customs receives shipment data before the package lands in the country, cutting processing delays and paperwork.</p>

		<title>Austria, Switzerland sign amending protocol to 1974 tax treaty</title>
		<link>https://regfollower.com/austria-switzerland-sign-amending-protocol-to-1974-tax-treaty/?utm_source=rss&#038;utm_medium=rss&#038;utm_campaign=austria-switzerland-sign-amending-protocol-to-1974-tax-treaty</link>

		<pubDate>Mon, 03 Aug 2026 12:58:07 +0000</pubDate>

		<category><![CDATA[Austria]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Europe]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Switzerland]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://regfollower.com/?p=85725</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[The Swiss State Secretariat for International Finance announced that Austria and Switzerland signed an amending protocol to their 1974 income and capital tax treaty on 30 July 2026. The protocol updates the treaty to implement the minimum standards on preventing double taxation and tax abuse and reflects changes since the previous revision under the 2009...]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>The Swiss State Secretariat for International Finance <a href="https://www.sif.admin.ch/en/switzerland-austria-protocol-dta" target="_blank" rel="noopener">announced</a> that Austria and Switzerland signed an amending protocol to their 1974 income and capital tax treaty on 30 July 2026.</p>
<p>The protocol updates the treaty to implement the minimum standards on preventing double taxation and tax abuse and reflects changes since the previous revision under the 2009 amending protocol. It is the sixth protocol to amend the treaty.</p>
<p>Key changes include:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Tax abuse rules</strong>: Introduction of a Principal Purpose Test (PPT) to deny treaty benefits where one of the principal purposes of an arrangement is to obtain those benefits. The treaty preamble is also updated to address tax evasion, tax avoidance and treaty shopping.</li>
<li><strong>Dividends: </strong>The maximum withholding tax rate remains 15%. A 0% withholding tax applies to dividends paid to companies holding at least 10% of the capital for at least 365 days. Pension funds and the two countries&#8217; national banks are also exempt.</li>
<li><strong>Permanent establishments:</strong> The protocol updates the rules for dependent agents and introduces anti-fragmentation measures for closely related enterprises.</li>
<li><strong>Tax collection:</strong> A new provision allows each country to assist the other in collecting tax claims.</li>
<li><strong>Exchange of information:</strong> Information exchange is expanded to cover all foreseeably relevant information for tax administration and enforcement, and bank secrecy cannot be used to refuse requests.</li>
</ul>
<p>The protocol will enter into force on the first day of the second month after the exchange of the instruments of ratification and will apply from 1 January of the year following its entry into force.</p>
<p><a href="https://regfollower.com/austria-approves-sixth-protocol-amending-1974-tax-treaty-with-switzerland/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Earlier</a>, the Austrian Council of Ministers approved the signing of the sixth protocol amending the 1974 income and capital tax treaty with Switzerland at its meeting on 1 July 2026.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Ukraine&#8217;s central bank has raised its key policy rate by 0.5 percentage points to 15.5%, effective 31 July 2026, citing persistent underlying inflationary pressures and expectations that headline inflation will accelerate further before easing.</p>
<p>The key policy rate is applied to calculate interest and penalties on late tax payments.</p>
<p>The National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) said the move is intended to support the attractiveness of hryvnia-denominated assets, maintain foreign exchange market stability and keep inflation expectations under control. The central bank forecasts consumer inflation will reach 10% by the end of 2026 before slowing to 6.9% in 2027 and returning to its 5% target by the end of 2028.</p>
<p>The NBU also upgraded its 2026 real GDP growth forecast to 1.8%, while warning that the ongoing war, intensified Russian attacks on infrastructure, and geopolitical risks in the Middle East remain the main threats to the economic outlook. It said it stands ready to tighten monetary policy further if inflationary pressures continue to build.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Mexico&#8217;s Tax Administration Service (Servicio de Administración Tributaria, SAT) has published an updated list of non-resident digital service providers registered for VAT purposes, with 286 entities included as of 30 June 2026. The update was issued through <a href="https://www.dof.gob.mx/nota_detalle.php?codigo=5794665&amp;fecha=24/07/2026#gsc.tab=0" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Official Letter No. 700 04 00 00 00 2026-077</a> published in the Official Gazette on 24 July 2026.</p>
<p>The updated register reflects compliance with the registration obligation under Article 18-D, section I, of the Value Added Tax Law, which applies to foreign residents without a permanent establishment in Mexico that provide digital services to users in the country.</p>
<p><strong>Nine new registrations and one removal</strong></p>
<p>The latest publication records 286 registered entities, compared with 278 in the second bimester of 2026, representing nine new registrations and one removal.</p>
<p>The newly added companies are:</p>
<ul>
<li>ALO, LLC.</li>
<li>Amazon Digital Germany GMBH.</li>
<li>Arlo Technologies, INC.</li>
<li>GPC Computer Software Limited.</li>
<li>Mainfunc Pte. LTD.</li>
<li>Match Group Americas, LLC.</li>
<li>Notion Labs, INC.</li>
<li>Quizlet, INC.</li>
</ul>
<p>The register also records the removal of Humor Rainbow, INC.</p>
<p><strong>Registration obligations</strong></p>
<p>Under Article 18-D of the Value Added Tax (IVA) Law, foreign residents without a permanent establishment in Mexico that supply digital services to recipients in the country are required to register with the Federal Taxpayers&#8217; Registry (Registro Federal de Contribuyentes, RFC).</p>
<p>Registered non-resident digital service providers are required to account for and collect VAT on the digital</p>
<p>services they supply in Mexico.</p>
<p>The SAT publishes the register every two months in the DOF and on its web portal to maintain transparency regarding taxpayers that have complied with the registration requirement.</p>
<p><strong>Information included in the register</strong></p>
<p>The register provides key identification details for each digital service provider, including:</p>
<ul>
<li>Corporate name (Denominación o razón social);</li>
<li>Trade name (Nombre comercial);</li>
<li>Country of origin;</li>
<li>Registration date in the RFC; and</li>
<li>RFC ID number (Clave en el RFC).</li>
</ul>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Greece has secured confirmation from the European Commission that the accreditation of its Paying Agency has been reinstated, marking the restoration of the country&#8217;s agricultural payments body after reforms implemented under an Action Plan covering September 2024 to March 2026. The agency now operates as the General Directorate of Audits, Aid and Payments (GDAAP) within the Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE).</p>
<p>The confirmation was included in an observation letter issued by the Directorate-General for Agriculture and Rural Development (DG AGRI) following an on-site audit conducted between 2 and 5 June 2026, which assessed the implementation of the Action Plan.</p>
<p>The Commission gave a positive assessment of several measures, including the increase in GDAAP&#8217;s established staffing positions to 775, plans to recruit 230 new employees with the intention of making those positions permanent, the completion of the selection and appointment of the Director General of GDAAP, the implementation of a conflict of interest management framework, and the development of an anti-fraud strategy together with the operation of a Risk Management Team.</p>
<p>The Commission also examined the integration of the former OPEKEPE into AADE and did not make any observations or recommendations regarding those integration measures.</p>
<p>While confirming the reinstatement of the accreditation, the Commission called for continued efforts to ensure the timely provision of information to the Certification Body, complete staffing, improve supervision of authorised bodies, and fully integrate the new risk management framework into the Management and Control System.</p>
<p>Minister of National Economy and Finance Kyriakos Pierrakakis said &#8220;The European Commission&#8217;s decision marks the restoration of the credibility of Greece&#8217;s agricultural payments system. We are building a system based on accountability, strong controls and modern procedures that protects Greek taxpayers, European resources and, above all, honest producers. Today&#8217;s development is an important vindication of our efforts, but it is not the end of the journey. We will continue with the same determination to ensure that every euro of support is paid promptly, fairly and with complete transparency to the rightful beneficiaries. Strong institutions mean credibility for the country and justice for its citizens.&#8221;</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Belgium&#8217;s Federal Public Service Finance has <a href="https://finances.belgium.be/fr/Actualites/avis-aux-debiteurs-du-precompte-professionnel-3" target="_blank" rel="noopener">published</a> the Royal Decree of 24 July 2026 in the Official Gazette on 30 July 2026, amending the rules governing the application of withholding tax. The decree introduces several important amendments to the rules for applying Annex III, particularly following the Law of 15 July 2026 reforming personal income tax.</p>
<p>The amendments concern:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Reduction for additional work:</strong> A general increase in the number of additional hours eligible for the withholding tax reduction to 180 hours across all sectors (No. 45.2 of Annex III).</li>
<li><strong>Employment bonus reduction:</strong> The &#8220;very low wage&#8221; component of the tax employment bonus has been increased from 52.54% to 63% (No. 46.2.2 of Annex III).</li>
<li><strong>Integration income (equivalent):</strong> Although integration income (equivalent) is now subject to taxation, no withholding tax is to be withheld from this income (No. 78.3.2 of Annex III).</li>
<li><strong>Young athletes:</strong> The minimum age for the first remuneration bracket has been lowered from 16 to 15 years, and the reference date of 1 January of the tax year has been corrected in the relevant rules (Nos. 139 and 144.1 of Annex III).</li>
</ul>
<p>In addition, the taxable portion of maintenance payments was reduced from 80% to 70% by the Law of 18 December 2025 containing various provisions. This change applies to maintenance payments made or awarded in 2025, provided that the taxable period in which they are received ends after 30 December 2025.</p>
<p>Alimony paid to non-residents is subject to withholding tax, and because that withholding is final, any overpayment normally can&#8217;t just be corrected later through an annual return. The 2025 rules taxed only 80% of the amount, but a gap remained for lump-sum payments: the Royal Decree of 14 February 2026 fixed the withholding rules for alimony paid in periodic instalments, leaving lump-sum payments still governed by the old rules.</p>
<p>The Royal Decree of 24 July 2026 closes that gap, extending the same fix to lump-sum alimony so recipients can get excess withholding refunded without delay.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Colombia’s National Tax and Customs Directorate (DIAN) has <a href="https://www.dian.gov.co/Prensa/Paginas/ng-dian-fortalece-seguridad-de-catalogo-de-factura-electronica.aspx" target="_blank" rel="noopener">introduced </a>a new validation mechanism for its Electronic Invoicing System from 28 July 2026, adding additional identity verification requirements for users accessing documents through the &#8220;Search Document&#8221; option.</p>
<p>The measure, announced by DIAN on 23 July 2026, is intended to strengthen the security of taxpayers&#8217; information and forms part of the authority&#8217;s ongoing efforts to promote safer digital environments for users.</p>
<p>Under the updated process, users searching for a document through the &#8220;Search Document&#8221; function will be required to enter the identification number of either the issuer or the recipient. Users wishing to download the document will be required to enter the same identification number again.</p>
<p>DIAN said users may encounter the message &#8220;Request blocked by security controls.&#8221; while using the search function. According to the authority, the message will appear when the system detects robots, automated processes or artificial intelligence agents that could overload the document search system and pose a risk to the security of information.</p>
<p>The authority said the appearance of the message does not indicate that access to the service has been suspended.</p>
<p>Where the message is displayed, the information system will require users to verify that they are human before allowing them to continue the operation through the system&#8217;s normal navigation process.</p>
<p>DIAN said the new validation mechanism forms part of the technical controls implemented to preserve the proper functioning of the Electronic Invoicing System platform.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Brazil&#8217;s Federal Revenue Service (Receita Federal) and the IBS Management Committee (CGIBS) will suspend the mandatory requirement to complete fields relating to the Contribution on Goods and Services (CBS) and the Tax on Goods and Services (IBS) in a range of electronic fiscal documents, as part of adjustments linked to the country&#8217;s Consumption Tax Reform.</p>

The changes are intended to accommodate the ongoing implementation of the Consumption Tax Reform while formally ratifying technical documentation that had previously been published.</p>
<p><strong>Validation rules amended</strong></p>

<p>The suspension of the mandatory fields will apply to several electronic fiscal document types, including NF-e, NFC-e, CT-e, CT-e OS, GTV-e, BP-e, NF3e and NFCom.</p>
<p><strong>Transition under tax reform</strong></p>
<p>The authorities said the changes are intended to support the implementation of Brazil&#8217;s Consumption Tax Reform by aligning document validation requirements with the evolving technical framework.</p>
<p>The Joint Technical Act will also formally approve the technical documentation that had already been released, providing a regulatory basis for the updated validation procedures.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>The European Commission has <a href="https://policy.trade.ec.europa.eu/news/eu-extends-suspension-eu-rebalancing-measures-against-united-states-2026-07-31_en" target="_blank" rel="noopener">adopted</a> an Implementing Regulation extending the suspension of EU rebalancing measures on US exports to the European Union on 31 July 2026. The decision means that the rebalancing measures, adopted last summer in the context of the risk of very high US tariffs on EU exports, will remain suspended without an end date.</p>
<p>The EU’s decision to suspend its rebalancing measures marks another important step in favour of greater certainty and stability in transatlantic trade, and the determination of the EU to implement what is set out in the EU–US Joint Statement of 21 August 2025.</p>
<p>The EU expects the US to fully honour its commitments as well under that Joint Statement.  In line with the provisions of the Implementing Regulation, the Commission will keep the suspension of the rebalancing measures under continuous review. In case it becomes necessary to defend the EU’s interest, the Commission may at any time take further action, including by reactivating these rebalancing measures.</p>
<p>The EU rebalancing measures were adopted on 24 July 2025, via <a href="https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2025/1564/oj/eng" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Commission Implementing Regulation 2025/1564</a>, in response to the US threats of very high US tariffs, and in case no negotiated solution could be achieved. The package of measures covered EUR 93 billion of EU imports from the US and imposed an export restriction for 95 million of EU exports to the US.</p>
<p>Following the successful <a href="https://regfollower.com/us-eu-finalise-trade-agreement-featuring-15-tariff-on-imports/">meeting</a> between Presidents Von Der Leyen and Trump in Turnberry on 27 July 2025 and the announcement of the political arrangement, which avoided the very high US tariff increases, the EU suspended the application of the package.</p>
<p>The adopted Commission Implementing Regulation will ensure the seamless continuation of the suspension adopted earlier this year via  Commission Implementing Regulation 2026/295, which was set to expire on 6 August 2026.</p>
<p><a href="https://regfollower.com/eu-halts-trade-countermeasures-following-us-agreement/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Earlier</a>,  the European Union published Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1727 of 5 August 2025 in the Official Journal of the European Union on 5 August 2025, which suspended the commercial rebalancing measures introduced by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1564 of 24 July 2025.</p>

The new rules, issued by the Ministry of Finance under Decision No. 616/1,...]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>The Lebanese Ministry of Finance issued new rules governing the exceptional tax on profits from US dollar purchases made through the former Sayrafa platform, increasing the eligibility threshold while detailing how taxpayers, banks and the tax administration must comply with the measure.</p>
<p>The new rules, issued by the Ministry of Finance under<a href="https://www.aldic.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/MoF-decision-616-1-dated-29-June-2026-Application-of-article-52-of-Budget-law-2026-on-Sayrafa-tax.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener"> Decision No. 616/1</a>, also set out filing, reporting, payment and refund requirements for transactions carried out between 2021 and 2023.</p>
<p><strong>Scope and threshold</strong></p>
<p>The 17% additional exceptional tax on net profits applies to any natural or legal person whose aggregate purchases of US dollars through the Sayrafa platform exceeded USD 100,000 during 2021, 2022 and 2023.</p>
<p>For determining whether the threshold has been reached, all accounts belonging to the same depositor are treated as a single account, while an individual&#8217;s share in joint accounts is included in the total.</p>
<p>The tax applies regardless of whether the individual or legal entity is otherwise subject to income tax.</p>
<p><strong>Tax rate and calculation</strong></p>
<p>The tax is levied at 17% of the taxable profit.</p>
<p>Taxable profit is calculated as the difference between the net amount paid in Lebanese pounds for the US dollars and their actual net value in Lebanese pounds on the transaction date, after deducting bank commissions and other amounts retained by the bank.</p>
<p><strong>Exemptions</strong></p>
<p>Transactions relating exclusively to the conversion of salaries and wages into US dollars through the Sayrafa platform under Central Bank circulars are excluded from the tax.</p>
<p><strong>Filing and reporting requirements</strong></p>
<p>Covered taxpayers must submit a separate declaration and pay the tax within two months of the publication of the decision.</p>
<p>Declarations must be submitted in paper form exclusively through LibanPost using Form T5, while Form S18 serves as the payment notice.</p>
<p>Commercial banks must provide the Ministry of Finance with comprehensive electronic data, in Excel format, covering all relevant Sayrafa transactions within the same two-month period.</p>
<p><strong>Payment methods</strong></p>
<p>Tax payments may be made through banks, LibanPost, or approved electronic payment providers, including OMT, Whish Money, B.O.B, and Cash Plus.</p>
<p>Refunds and recalculations</p>
<p>Taxpayers who previously paid the tax but whose aggregate Sayrafa purchases did not exceed the new USD 100,000 threshold may apply for a refund.</p>
<p>Taxpayers whose purchases exceed the threshold may also recalculate their tax liability and claim a refund of any excess tax where bank commissions and deductions were not previously taken into account.</p>
<p><strong>Penalties</strong></p>
<p>Late filing is subject to a penalty of 10% of the tax due for each month of delay.</p>
<p>Late payment is subject to a penalty of 2% of the tax due for each month of delay.</p>
<p>The decision entered into force upon publication and repealed Decision No. 647/1 of 4 June 2024.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Lebanon&#8217;s Ministry of Finance (MoF) has issued <a href="https://www.aldic.net/mof-decision-6421-dated-10-july-2026-reduction-of-penalties-till-30-december-2026/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Decision No. 642/1 on 10 July 2026</a>, granting reductions in tax penalties for eligible tax assessments issued from 16 November 2022, the publication date of the 2022 Budget Law.</p>
<p>The measure, issued under Article 22 of Law No. 10 (Budget Law 2022), applies regardless of when the underlying tax infringement occurred, provided the assessment was issued on or after that date.</p>
<p>The decision allows taxpayers to benefit from the penalty reductions until 30 December 2026, subject to meeting the applicable settlement conditions.</p>
<p><strong>Taxes covered</strong></p>
<p>The penalty reduction applies to taxes and fees administered by the Directorate General of Public Finance. Covered direct taxes include income tax, built property tax, inheritance tax, and offshore and petroleum-related taxes.</p>
<p>The measure also covers indirect taxes, including Value Added Tax (VAT), stamp duties, and specific fees imposed on products such as alcohol, tobacco, cement and soft drinks.</p>
<p><strong>Penalty reduction rates</strong></p>
<p>The level of relief depends on the type of tax and the nature of the penalty.</p>
<p>For most taxes, proportional verification penalties are reduced by 85%, flat-rate verification penalties by 60%, and collection penalties by 75%.</p>
<p>For additional assessments relating to VAT and salary or wage tax, proportional verification penalties are reduced by 50%, flat-rate verification penalties by 60%, and collection penalties by 50%.</p>
<p>No reduction is available for penalties relating to VAT and salary or wage tax self-assessments.</p>
<p><strong>Eligibility conditions and exclusions</strong></p>
<p>To qualify for the reductions, taxpayers must pay both the reduced penalty and the underlying tax within the period specified in the decision and no later than 30 December 2026.</p>
<p>The reductions do not apply to penalties below LBP 200,000, or below USD 3 or EUR 3 for taxes denominated in foreign currency. They also exclude penalties where the principal tax was not paid within the statutory deadline and penalties already covered by special settlement laws.</p>
<p>The decision further states that penalties paid before its issuance are considered final revenue of the Treasury and are not refundable.</p>
<p>Where the value of a penalty reduction exceeds LBP 60 billion – or approximately USD 667,000, approval from the Council of Ministers is required.</p>
<p><strong>Administrative procedures</strong></p>
<p>Under the decision, the Department of Collection will issue revised payment orders reflecting the reduced penalties for eligible taxpayers.</p>
<p>Taxpayers who fail to pay both the reduced penalty and the corresponding tax within the prescribed period will forfeit their right to benefit from the settlement measures.</p>

		<title>Malaysia issues transfer pricing guidelines for intra-group loans</title>
		<link>https://regfollower.com/malaysia-issues-transfer-pricing-guidelines-for-intra-group-loans/?utm_source=rss&#038;utm_medium=rss&#038;utm_campaign=malaysia-issues-transfer-pricing-guidelines-for-intra-group-loans</link>

				<category><![CDATA[Application to intra-group services]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Definition of control]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[General]]></category>

					<description><![CDATA[Malaysia&#8217;s Inland Revenue Board (IRBM) has published the Malaysia Transfer Pricing Guidelines for Intra-Group Loans (MFTIL), providing a comprehensive framework for determining whether financing transactions between associated persons comply with the arm&#8217;s length principle. The guidelines No. 3/2026, published on 30 July 2026, outline how taxpayers should assess, price and document intra-group loan arrangements. Arm&#8217;s...]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Malaysia&#8217;s Inland Revenue Board (IRBM) has published the Malaysia Transfer Pricing Guidelines for Intra-Group Loans (MFTIL), providing a comprehensive framework for determining whether financing transactions between associated persons comply with the arm&#8217;s length principle.</p>
<p>The <a href="https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/Malaysia-Transfer-Pricing-Guidelines-Controlled-Financial-Transactions-Intra-Group-Loans.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener">guidelines No. 3/2026</a>, published on 30 July 2026, outline how taxpayers should assess, price and document intra-group loan arrangements.</p>
<p><strong>Arm&#8217;s length principle and transaction delineation</strong></p>
<p>The guidelines state that the actual nature of a financial transaction must be determined based on its economic substance rather than its legal form or contractual label. Taxpayers are required to examine factors including risk control, functional contributions and the actual conduct of the parties when delineating financial transactions.</p>
<p>A central feature of the guidance is the distinction between debt and equity. The IRBM explains that a purported loan must be assessed to determine whether it represents a genuine loan or a contribution to equity capital. Among the factors to be considered are the existence of a fixed maturity date, voting rights and a legal obligation to repay the funds.</p>
<p>The guidance also provides for recharacterisation where a transaction is considered commercially irrational or lacks the characteristics of a genuine loan. In such cases, the Director General of Inland Revenue (DGIR) may disregard or recharacterise the arrangement, potentially resulting in the disallowance of interest deductions.</p>
<p><strong>Assessing lenders, borrowers and creditworthiness</strong></p>
<p>The MFTIL requires taxpayers to evaluate intra-group loans from both the lender&#8217;s and the borrower&#8217;s perspectives. This includes assessing the lender&#8217;s credit analysis of the borrower as well as whether the borrower sought financing that is commercially appropriate and cost-effective.</p>
<p>Creditworthiness assessments are expected to rely on recognised credit ratings, including those issued by agencies such as RAM Ratings, Moody&#8217;s and S&amp;P, to evaluate default risk.</p>
<p>The guidelines also address the effect of group membership on borrowing costs. They recognise the concept of implicit support, under which a subsidiary may obtain more favourable financing terms simply because it belongs to a multinational enterprise (MNE) group. According to the guidance, this inherent benefit generally does not require a transfer pricing adjustment.</p>
<p><strong>Transfer pricing methods</strong></p>
<p>The guidelines outline several approaches for determining arm&#8217;s length interest rates.</p>
<p>The Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP) Method is identified as the preferred method where reliable market data for comparable loans is available.</p>
<p>Where appropriate, taxpayers may instead apply the Cost of Funds Method, which calculates an arm&#8217;s length rate by combining the lender&#8217;s borrowing cost with an appropriate risk premium and profit margin. The guidance notes that this method is particularly relevant for intermediary entities that on-lend funds within a corporate group.</p>
<p>To reduce compliance costs, the IRBM has also introduced a simplified method for eligible taxpayers. Under this approach, taxpayers may apply designated interest rates published by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM), specifically the Deposit Rate or the Average Lending Rate (ALR), provided the aggregate amount of intra-group loans does not exceed MYR 50 million.</p>
<p><strong>Documentation and compliance obligations</strong></p>
<p>The MFTIL requires taxpayers to maintain Contemporaneous Transfer Pricing Documentation (CTPD) to demonstrate that interest rates applied to intra-group loans comply with the arm&#8217;s length principle. Supporting documentation should include loan agreements, credit assessments and other relevant evidence.</p>
<p>The guidance requires taxpayers to retain all relevant records, including CTPD, for seven years. Although the documentation does not have to be submitted with the tax return, it must be provided within 14 days of a written request from the DGIR.</p>
<p>The guidelines also address Section 140B of the Income Tax Act 1967, which contains provisions governing loans or advances made to directors.</p>
<p>The publication of the MFTIL establishes a dedicated framework for evaluating related-party financing arrangements in Malaysia, setting out the IRBM&#8217;s expectations on transaction characterisation, transfer pricing methodologies and supporting documentation for intra-group loans.</p>
]]></content:encoded>

		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Abdur Rouf]]></dc:creator>

				<category><![CDATA[Scope of GMT]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Europe]]></category>

		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://regfollower.com/?p=85687</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[The UK’s His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs (HMRC) has updated its Pillar Two guidance to confirm the adoption of the OECD’s transitional approach for the central filing and exchange of the GloBE Information Return (GIR). Under the updated framework, eligible multinational groups that centrally file their GIR in a participating jurisdiction and submit a timely...]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>The UK’s His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs (HMRC) has updated its Pillar Two <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/global-information-return-filing-and-exchange-transitional-approach/global-information-return-gir-filing-and-exchange-transitional-approach" target="_blank" rel="noopener">guidance</a> to confirm the adoption of the OECD’s transitional approach for the central filing and exchange of the GloBE Information Return (GIR). Under the updated framework, eligible multinational groups that centrally file their GIR in a participating jurisdiction and submit a timely Overseas Return Notification (ORN) will generally not be required to submit a separate UK GIR.</p>
<p>Published on 29 July 2026, the revised guidance aligns the UK’s approach with the OECD’s transitional arrangements released earlier in 2026, providing greater clarity for groups facing their first Pillar Two reporting obligations. The measures also outline HMRC’s treatment of local filing requirements, deadlines, and penalties during the transition period.</p>
<p><strong>Applicability</strong></p>
<p>The transitional approach applies where the filing deadline for the GloBE Information Return (GIR) is no later than 31 December 2026. Where the GIR is centrally filed in one of the participating jurisdictions and HMRC receives the relevant GIR information from the overseas authority within six months of the filing deadline, HMRC will not enforce local filing of the GIR and will reduce certain penalties to nil.</p>
<p>To benefit from the arrangements, groups must submit an Overseas Return Notification (ORN) to HMRC on time. An ORN is regarded as submitted on time if it is filed before any late filing penalties arise, taking into account HMRC&#8217;s transitional approach to late filing penalties. The ORN must specify the date the GIR was filed overseas. However, where software issues prevent the GIR from being filed overseas before the ORN is due, the group should still submit the ORN on time using a notional GIR filing date of 1 January 2026.</p>
<p><strong>Local filing switch off</strong></p>
<p>HMRC said that where a GIR has been centrally filed in one of the participating jurisdictions and a timely ORN has been submitted, it will generally not require a separate information return to be filed in the UK.</p>
<p>The guidance notes that the UK&#8217;s GIR filing portal opened on 19 May 2026. HMRC has directed groups to its guidance on reporting Pillar Two Top-up Taxes and selecting appropriate software for submitting ORNs and GIRs.</p>
<p><strong>Penalties</strong></p>
<p>An ORN is valid only if, at the time it is submitted, the GIR has already been filed in an overseas jurisdiction that has an agreement with HMRC to exchange the information contained in the GIR. Ordinarily, submitting an invalid ORN would leave the group&#8217;s obligation to file a GIR in the UK unchanged, and failure to submit the return on time could result in late filing penalties.</p>
<p>However, because all participating jurisdictions have indicated their intention to enter into an agreement to exchange GIR information with HMRC, the authority said it will initially reduce the late filing penalty for the GIR to zero where a timely ORN names one of those jurisdictions.</p>
<p><strong>Failure to receive the GIR on exchange</strong></p>
<p>If HMRC does not receive the centrally filed GIR within six months of the filing deadline, it may contact the group to enforce the local filing requirement in the UK. In such cases, late filing penalties may begin to accrue until the group&#8217;s UK filing obligations have been met.</p>
<p><strong>Central filing in the UK</strong></p>
<p>The tax authority said businesses requiring information on submitting an ORN and GIR in the UK should refer to the <a href="https://www.gov.uk/guidance/how-to-report-pillar-2-top-up-taxes" target="_blank" rel="noopener">How to report Pillar Two Top-up Taxes</a> and <a href="https://www.gov.uk/guidance/choose-the-right-software-for-pillar-2-top-up-taxes" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Choose the right software for Pillar Two Top-up Taxes</a> guidance pages.</p>
<p><strong>Jurisdictions</strong></p>
<p>The transitional approach applies where the GIR is centrally filed in any of the following jurisdictions:</p>
<p>Australia, Austria, Barbados, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Gibraltar, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Republic of Korea, Romania, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Slovenia, South Africa and Turkey.</p>

					<description><![CDATA[The US Internal Revenue Service (IRS) has issued Revenue Procedure 2026-28, exempting certain foreign FIFA member associations that participated in the FIFA World Cup 2026 from filing  US Federal Form 990 (Return of Organisation Exempt From Income Tax) for tax years in which they have no US-source or effectively connected income other than income earned...]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>The US Internal Revenue Service (IRS) has issued <a href="https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-26-28.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Revenue Procedure 2026-28</a>, exempting certain foreign FIFA member associations that participated in the FIFA World Cup 2026 from filing  <a href="https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-990" target="_blank" rel="noopener">US Federal Form 990</a> (Return of Organisation Exempt From Income Tax) for tax years in which they have no US-source or effectively connected income other than income earned from participating in the tournament.</p>
<p>Under these rules, qualifying foreign participating member associations (PMAs) are relieved from filing annual information returns provided their US-sourced income is derived solely from tournament participation. This exception covers various financial gains, such as FIFA prize money and related promotional revenue, for tax years starting in 2025.</p>
<p>By exercising its discretionary authority, the Treasury Department aims to simplify tax compliance for teams whose global operations are otherwise unrelated to the domestic tax system.</p>
<p>The Treasury and IRS identified three primary reasons why annual Form 990 filings for foreign PMAs are unnecessary:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Discrete and time-limited activity: </strong>Foreign PMAs are not expected to generate recurring US-source or effectively connected income (ECI) due to the temporary nature of the tournament.</li>
<li><strong>Membership-based presence:</strong> A PMA’s physical or economic presence in the United States stems from its membership in FIFA and tournament participation (along with incidental financial and administrative setups), rather than independent commercial activity in the US.</li>
<li><strong>Disproportionate compliance burden:</strong> Form 990 requires an organisation to report its worldwide operations. Requiring foreign PMAs to file would create a heavy administrative burden that far outweighs the informational benefit to the IRS, given that PMAs operate overwhelmingly outside the US.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Qualification requirements</strong></p>
<p>To be eligible for filing relief under RP 2026-28 for a given taxable year, a foreign FIFA association must meet four criteria:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>World Cup participation: </strong>The national team of the foreign PMA must actively compete in the FIFA World Cup 2026.</li>
<li><strong>Foreign entity status:</strong> The organisation must qualify as a foreign entity (not created or organised in the US or under US law).</li>
<li>Tax-exempt status: The organisation must substantively qualify for federal tax exemption under IRC section 501(a).</li>
<li><strong>Income limitations: </strong>The PMA must have no gross income from US sources and no gross income effectively connected with a US trade or business, other than income directly related to competing in the tournament.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Scope of relief and covered forms</strong></p>
<p>For qualifying foreign PMAs, RP 2026-28 provides the following relief on an annual, taxable-year basis:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Form 990/990-EZ:</strong> Qualifying FIFA member associations are exempt from filing annual Form 990 or Form 990-EZ.</li>
<li><strong>Form 990-N:</strong> They are also exempt from filing the annual Form 990-N (e-Postcard).</li>
<li><strong>Automatic relief:</strong> The exemption applies automatically, even without an IRS determination letter recognising Section 501(a) tax-exempt status.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Qualifying income vs. non-qualifying income</strong></p>
<p>The revenue procedure establishes clear boundaries regarding permissible income during tournament years:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Relief retained: </strong>Qualifying FIFA member associations keep the filing exemption if their only US-related income is directly tied to FIFA World Cup 2026 participation (e.g., FIFA prize money or tournament-related sponsorship income).</li>
<li><strong>Relief lost: </strong>The exemption does not apply if the association earns any US-source or effectively connected income unrelated to the World Cup, requiring it to meet normal Form 990/990-EZ filing obligations unless another exception applies.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Explicit inclusions &amp; statutory exclusions</strong></p>
<p>The filing relief applies only to qualifying FIFA participating member associations and excludes private foundations and section 509(a)(3) supporting organisations. It is limited to organisational information return filings and does not affect the US tax, withholding, employment tax, treaty, or state and local tax obligations of individual players, coaches, contractors, or support staff.</p>
<p>Revenue Procedure 2026-28 took effect on 24 July 2026 and applies to taxable years beginning on or after 1 January 2025.</p>

<p><strong>Five-year record retention requirement</strong></p>
<p>The NTBNA also reminded consumers that where goods or services sold under an electronic invoice are later returned or discounted through a website, telephone or other electronic means, both parties should retain the agreement messages and supporting documentation for at least five years.</p>

<p><strong>Guidance period has ended</strong></p>

<p>With the transition period now over, the NTBNA urged businesses to ensure both parties have reached agreement before transmitting the relevant allowance note information to the E-Invoice Platform for record-keeping, in line with the applicable regulations, to avoid penalties for late or inaccurate reporting.</p>
<p>The bureau said further information is available in the Electronic Invoice Information Record-keeping Promotion Area under the Hot Topics section of its website.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>France has postponed the transfer of Value Added Tax (VAT) provisions from the General Tax Code (CGI) to the Code des impositions sur les biens et services (CIBS) until 1 January 2027 under <a href="https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/download/pdf?id=cdCQzxZaAzC_jotuadKSBmLCXpWGQoisGfxBVdPuq_E=" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Ordinance No. 2026-671 of 27 July 2026, published in the Official Journal on 28 July</a>. The ordinance amends Ordinance No. 2025-1247 of 17 December 2025, which had scheduled the recodification to take effect on 1 September 2026.</p>
<p>Until 31 December 2026, the VAT provisions and references contained in the General Tax Code (CGI), including those governing real estate VAT and VAT on rents, will continue to apply. From 1 January 2027, they will be replaced by the corresponding provisions in the Code des impositions sur les biens et services (CIBS). The report accompanying the ordinance does not provide any exception for real estate VAT.</p>
<p><strong>Clarifications to the VAT framework</strong></p>
<p>In addition to postponing the implementation date, the ordinance refines the recodified VAT framework by clarifying definitions and operational rules. It updates the treatment of taxable transactions, intra-European deliveries, imports, provision of services and the place of operation. The ordinance also confirms that the taxable base generally consists of the total consideration received by the supplier, including monetary and in-kind payments, while setting out specific rules for single-use and multi-use vouchers and for imported goods based on customs value.</p>
<p><strong>Liability, deductions and sector-specific rules</strong></p>
<p>The ordinance maintains existing provisions on VAT rates, exemptions and liability. It preserves reduced, very reduced, zero and special VAT rates for eligible goods and services, as well as exemptions covering intra-European deliveries, exports, specified humanitarian aid and certain imported personal belongings. It also confirms reverse charge provisions, joint liability rules for certain travail à façon arrangements, proportional (prorata) VAT deduction methods and sector-specific regimes for agriculture, second-hand goods, investment gold, travel operators and copyright royalties.</p>
<p><strong>Administrative obligations remain</strong></p>
<p>The updated framework also maintains VAT administrative requirements, including invoicing, record-keeping and reporting obligations. Taxable persons must continue to issue invoices containing mandatory VAT information, maintain registers for intra-European movements of goods and specified transactions, and submit data required by the tax authorities to verify VAT liability. The postponement provides businesses with additional time to prepare for the migration of VAT legislation to the CIBS, while leaving the substance of the recodified framework largely intact ahead of its application from 1 January 2027.</p>

<li><strong> Who should read this information bulletin?</strong></li>
</ol>
<p>Anyone who is responsible for the tax affairs of a small business operation (referred to as &#8216;small business&#8217;) and wants to understand:</p>
<ul>
<li>When should a small business register for Corporate Tax?</li>
<li>What are the exceptions to the requirement of registering for Corporate Tax?</li>
<li>What is the Corporate Tax rate for small business?</li>
<li>Which special reliefs are available to small business?</li>
<li>What are the conditions to be eligible for Small Business Relief?</li>
<li>How to make an election for Small Business Relief?</li>
<li>What are the other compliance requirements for small business under the Corporate Tax Law?</li>
</ul>
<ol start="2">
<li><strong> When should a small business register for Corporate Tax?</strong></li>
</ol>
<p>All Taxable Persons must register for Corporate Tax with the Federal Tax Authority (&#8220;FTA&#8221;) on EmaraTax1 within the prescribed time limit. A small business is considered to be a Taxable Person under the Corporate Tax Law if it conducts a Business or Business Activity and meets the conditions to be a Resident Person or Non-Resident Person.</p>
<p>The timeline for registration depends on whether the small business is conducted by a natural person or a juridical person and whether it meets the conditions to be a Resident Person or a Non-Resident Person for Corporate Tax purposes. This also applies to Free Zone Persons.</p>
<p>For example, the timeline for registration for a small business who is a juridical person and a Resident Person is as follows:</p>
<ul>
<li>A juridical person that is incorporated or otherwise established or recognised under the applicable legislation in the UAE, including a Free Zone Person: Deadline for submitting a Tax Registration application &#8211; Three months from the date of incorporation, establishment or recognition of the juridical person.</li>
<li>A juridical person that is incorporated or otherwise established or recognised under the applicable legislation of a foreign jurisdiction that is effectively managed and controlled in the UAE: Deadline for submitting a Tax Registration application &#8211; Three months from the end of the Financial Year of the juridical person.</li>
</ul>
<p>For more information on the timeline to register for Corporate Tax for other types of Taxable Persons, please refer to the relevant FTA Decision and Public Clarification published on the FTA&#8217;s website.</p>
<ol start="3">
<li><strong> Are there any exceptions to the requirement to register for Corporate Tax for small businesses?</strong></li>
</ol>
<p>A natural person who conducts a Business or Business Activity in the UAE is only required to register for Corporate Tax if the total Turnover from such Business or Business Activities exceeds AED 1 million within a Gregorian calendar year.</p>
<p>For more information on the taxation of natural persons under Corporate Tax Law, please refer to the guidance published on the FTA&#8217;s website.</p>
<p>*Note: The AED 1 million registration threshold for natural persons is separate from the AED 3 million Revenue threshold for Small Business Relief (see section 6)</p>
<ol start="4">
<li>What is the Corporate Tax rate applicable to a small business?</li>
</ol>
<p>There is no special Corporate Tax rate applicable for a small business.</p>
<p>The Taxable Income will be subject to standard Corporate Tax at the following rates:</p>
<ul>
<li>0% on the portion of the Taxable Income not exceeding AED 375,000; and</li>
<li>9% on the portion of the Taxable Income that exceeds AED 375,000.</li>
</ul>
<p>The Corporate Tax rates above also apply when the total Turnover derived by a natural person from its Business or Business Activities in the UAE in a Gregorian calendar year exceeds AED 1 million, starting from Gregorian calendar year 2024.</p>
<ol start="5">
<li><strong> Are there any special reliefs available to small businesses?</strong></li>
</ol>
<p>A small business that is a Taxable Person and a Resident Person may be eligible to make an election for Small Business Relief.</p>
<p>Where a valid Small Business Relief election is made, the compliance obligations are reduced as follows:</p>
<ul>
<li>Ordinarily, Taxable Persons would calculate their Taxable Income by adjusting their Accounting Income for the Corporate Tax treatment of certain income and expenditure. By contrast, Small Business Relief treats eligible Taxable Persons as having no Taxable Income for the relevant Tax Period and, therefore, they do not need to calculate their Taxable Income or pay Corporate Tax.</li>
<li>Benefit of preparing a simplified Tax Return.</li>
<li>Simplified record keeping requirements, including the ability to prepare their Financial Statements based on the cash basis of accounting.</li>
</ul>
<ol start="6">
<li><strong> What are the conditions to be eligible for Small Business Relief?</strong></li>
</ol>
<p>To be eligible for Small Business Relief, the small business must meet all of the below conditions:</p>
<ul>
<li>Be a Taxable Person (including a natural person).</li>
<li>Be a Resident Person.</li>
<li>The Revenue must be equal to or below AED 3 million in a relevant Tax Period and in each for the previous Tax Periods that end on or before 31 December 2026. Businesses should monitor any updates by the Ministry of Finance and the FTA for post-2026 provisions.</li>
<li>Cannot be a member of a Multinational Enterprise Group as defined in Cabinet Resolution No. 44 of 2020, nor be a Qualifying Free Zone Person.</li>
</ul>
<p>For further information on who is eligible for Small Business Relief, and the consequences of making a Small Business Relief election, please refer to the relevant Ministerial Decision and guidance published on the FTA&#8217;s website.</p>
<ol start="7">
<li><strong> How to make an election for Small Business Relief?</strong></li>
</ol>
<p>Eligible Taxable Persons that meet the conditions for Small Business Relief and wish to benefit from it must first register for Corporate Tax purposes. Thereafter, they must make an election in their Tax Return in order to benefit from this relief. This election must be made for each Tax Period for which a Tax Return is filed in order for the relief to apply for that Tax Period.</p>
<p>For further information on the Small Business Relief election, please refer to the guidance published on the FTA&#8217;s website.</p>
<ol start="8">
<li><strong> What is the Corporate Tax filing requirement?</strong></li>
</ol>
<p>All Taxable Persons must file a Tax Return or a simplified Tax Return (in case of Small Business Relief election) via EmaraTax, no later than nine months from the end of the relevant Tax Period.</p>
<p>For further information on how to file a Tax Return, please refer to the guidance published on the FTA&#8217;s website.</p>
<ol start="9">
<li><strong> Are small businesses required to maintain any records?</strong></li>
</ol>
<p>All Businesses are required to maintain records and documents for a period of seven years following the end of the Tax Period to which they relate. Such records and documents should:</p>
<ul>
<li>Support any information provided in a Tax Return, or in any other document that is filed with the FTA</li>
<li>Enable the FTA to readily ascertain the Taxable Person&#8217;s Taxable Income calculation</li>
</ul>
<p>Records and documents to be maintained typically include:</p>
<ul>
<li>Financial Statements (which must be audited in specific situations)</li>
<li>Bank statements</li>
<li>Loan or financing documentation</li>
<li>Sales and purchase ledgers</li>
<li>Invoices or other records of daily earnings, such as till rolls</li>
<li>Purchase orders and delivery notes</li>
<li>Other relevant business correspondence</li>
</ul>
<ol start="10">
<li><strong> Are there any penalties imposed in case of non-compliance with Corporate Tax Law?</strong></li>
</ol>
<p>Administrative Penalties may be imposed for non-compliance with the Corporate Tax Law. It is, therefore, important that all Taxable Persons register for Corporate Tax purposes, file accurate Tax Returns and pay any Corporate Tax due by the relevant deadlines.</p>
<p>For more information on penalties applicable for Corporate Tax purposes, please refer to the relevant Cabinet Decision that is available on the FTA&#8217;s website.</p>
]]></content:encoded>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Australia&#8217;s Department of Industry, Science and Resources opened a <a href="https://consult.industry.gov.au/cmpti-draft-forms-timeframes-and-guidance" target="_blank" rel="noopener">public consultation</a> on 14 July 2026 on the proposed application and reporting arrangements for the Critical Minerals Production Tax Incentive (CMPTI), inviting stakeholder feedback on draft registration and reporting form questions, annual reporting and registration transfer timeframes, and customer guidance.</p>
<p>The consultation is intended to ensure that the administrative framework is clear, practical and proportionate while supporting compliance with Division 419 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 before the incentive comes into effect in 2027.</p>
<p>The CMPTI forms part of the Australian Government&#8217;s Future Made in Australia plan. Under the scheme, eligible companies will receive a refundable tax offset equal to 10% of eligible Australian processing costs for critical minerals processed and refined between 1 July 2027 and 30 June 2040, with support available for up to 10 years per project.</p>
<p>The department is seeking submissions from industry participants, advisers, governments, community groups and regulators on proposed application and reporting form questions, annual reporting and registration transfer timeframes, and customer guidance.</p>
<p><strong>Registration requirements</strong></p>
<p>The consultation paper proposes a registration process designed to confirm an applicant&#8217;s identity and eligibility for the incentive.</p>
<p>Applicants would be required to provide company details, including their Australian Business Number (ABN), registered business name and head office addresses. They would also need to confirm that they are a constitutional corporation, understand the tax offset period, and meet residency requirements and the Community Benefit Rules.</p>
<p>For projects operated through joint ventures, the proposed registration forms would collect information on shared ownership arrangements, including partner names, ownership percentages and cost-sharing arrangements.</p>
<p><strong>Activity eligibility</strong></p>
<p>The consultation also covers proposed questions to assess whether an applicant&#8217;s activities meet the legislative definition of critical mineral processing.</p>
<p>The framework focuses on the substantial transformation of feedstock containing a critical mineral into a purer, chemically distinct form through extractive metallurgy.</p>
<p>Specific questions have been proposed for three regulated processing categories.</p>
<p>For High Purity Alumina (HPA), applicants would need to demonstrate transformation into HPA with a purity of at least 99.99%.</p>
<p>For graphite processing, applicants would be required to provide information on outcomes such as increased graphitic carbon content, reduced particle size or more spherical particle shapes.</p>
<p>For Precursor Cathode Active Material (pCAM), applicants would need to demonstrate chemical transformation into material suitable for lithium-ion battery cathodes.</p>
<p>The consultation paper also clarifies that mining, beneficiation activities such as crushing and grinding, and manufacturing activities are excluded from the incentive.</p>
<p><strong>Reporting and compliance framework</strong></p>
<p>The proposed arrangements include ongoing reporting obligations and processes for managing changes to registered projects.</p>
<p>Companies would be required to submit annual reports covering actual production volumes for critical and non-critical mineral outputs, as well as projected production for the following year.</p>
<p>The framework would also establish procedures for notifying the department of changes to facilities, ownership structures or joint venture arrangements, and for transferring registrations to other entities.</p>
<p>The proposals include provisions for late submissions where delays occur due to circumstances outside an applicant&#8217;s control, along with procedures for requesting internal reviews of departmental decisions.</p>
<p>The department said the proposed questions are intended to collect information needed to assess eligibility and support ongoing compliance while ensuring the application process remains practical for industry participants.</p>
<p>The consultation will close on 11 August 2026.</p>

The measure, signed by the Director of the Italian Revenue Agency on 30 July 2026, provides guidance for employers seeking...]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>The Italian Revenue Agency has <a href="https://www.fiscooggi.it/portale/-/bonus-e-stock-options-variabili-come-evitare-l-addizionale-del-10-" target="_blank" rel="noopener">issued</a> a measure setting out the practical rules for claiming tax relief on bonuses and variable remuneration paid in the form of bonuses and stock options in the financial sector.</p>
<p>The measure, signed by the Director of the Italian Revenue Agency on 30 July 2026, provides guidance for employers seeking to benefit from the relief introduced by the 2026 Budget Law.</p>
<p>The relief applies to remuneration paid to executives and individuals engaged under coordinated and continuous collaboration agreements.</p>
<p>The measure implements Article 1, paragraph 137, of Law No. 199/2025, which inserted paragraph 2-ter into Article 33 of Decree-Law No. 78/2010. Under the new provision, where the statutory requirements are satisfied, the 10% additional tax on variable remuneration exceeding the fixed portion of salary does not apply to eligible taxpayers.</p>
<p>Paragraph 2-ter also required the Director of the Italian Revenue Agency to issue implementation rules setting out how eligible taxpayers may access the relief.</p>
<p><strong>Relief dependent on donations to Third Sector entities</strong></p>
<p>The guidance states that access to the preferential tax regime is conditional on the payer of the variable remuneration making a payment to one or more Third Sector entities governed by Legislative Decree No. 117/2017 (Third Sector Code).</p>
<p>The payment must equal at least twice the total amount of the additional tax due for the relevant tax period. The calculation must be based on the full amount of the additional tax that would otherwise be payable.</p>
<p>The measure also requires the recipient organisations to be independent of the payer. As a result, entities that control the donor, are controlled by the donor, or belong to the same group under common control are not eligible to receive the qualifying payments.</p>
<p><strong>Payment rules and additional contribution option</strong></p>
<p>According to the guidance, donations qualifying for the relief must generally be made by bank transfer.</p>
<p>However, payments made before the publication of the measure using other methods will also be recognised, provided they are traceable and properly recorded by the beneficiary entity.</p>
<p>The measure also provides a safeguard where year-end adjustments show that the amount already paid falls below the statutory minimum of twice the additional tax due. In those circumstances, the payer may preserve the relief by making an additional payment to the Third Sector entities within 60 days from the deadline established by Article 4, paragraph 6-quater, of Presidential Decree No. 322/1998 for submission of the Certificazione Unica.</p>
<p><strong>Reporting and record-keeping obligations</strong></p>
<p>Employers granting eligible stock options and bonuses must include in their income tax return both the total value of the qualifying payments and the tax identification numbers of the beneficiary entities.</p>
<p>They must also retain documentation demonstrating both the total additional tax due and the amounts actually paid.</p>
<p>In addition, the withholding agent must certify in the Certificazione Unica (CU) issued to executives and coordinated and continuous collaborators receiving the variable remuneration that the 10% additional tax rate has not been applied in accordance with Article 33, paragraph 2-ter.</p>
<p><strong>Effective date and transitional arrangements</strong></p>
<p>The implementation rules apply to variable remuneration paid from 1 January 2026.</p>
<p>As the Redditi income tax return form incorporating the new reporting requirements will only be approved in 2027, the measure introduces transitional arrangements for 2026.</p>
<p>Payments made from 1 January 2026 until the end of the tax period, where that tax period ends before 31 December 2026, must be reported in the Redditi form to be approved in 2027. The same return must also include payments made during the tax period in progress as of 31 December 2026.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Austria published the <a href="https://www.ris.bka.gv.at/Dokumente/BgblAuth/BGBLA_2026_I_62/BGBLA_2026_I_62.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Budget Accompanying Act 2027–2028</a> in the Official Gazette on 29 July 2026, introducing a broad package of tax, financial and policy measures under the country&#8217;s dual budget for 2027 and 2028.</p>
<p>The legislation includes a new parcel tax, changes to corporate and alcohol tax, updates to income tax relief and the stability levy for banks, alongside reforms covering pensions, labour, family support, environmental policy, justice and transport.</p>
<ol>
<li><strong><span style="text-decoration: underline">Financial and tax reforms</span></strong></li>
</ol>
<p>The Budget detail several significant changes to the Austrian tax and financial landscape:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Parcel tax:</strong> A new tax is introduced for the delivery of parcels from mail-order businesses. Starting 1 October 2026, a tax of EUR 2 per parcel will be charged to “mail-order retailers” whose domestic turnover exceeded EUR 100 million in the previous year.</li>
<li><strong>Corporate tax:</strong> While the standard corporate tax rate remains at 23%, a higher rate of 24% will be introduced for income exceeding EUR 1 million starting in 2028.</li>
<li><strong>Alcohol tax: </strong>The alcohol tax rate will increase to EUR 1,560 per 100 liters of pure alcohol, effective 1 January 2027.</li>
<li><strong>Income tax adjustments:</strong></li>
<li style="list-style-type: none">
<ul>
<li>Employees can claim up to EUR 300 annually for ergonomically suitable home office furniture (e.g., desks, chairs, lighting) starting in 2027.</li>
<li>The Family Bonus Plus rules are adjusted regarding how the bonus is split between parents depending on the age of the child and who receives family allowance [68–73].</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Stability levy for banks:</strong> The rates for the stability levy on credit institutions are adjusted for 2027–2029 (0.033% to 0.041%) and set for 2030 onwards (0.024% to 0.029%).</li>
</ul>
<ol start="2">
<li><span style="text-decoration: underline"><strong> Social affairs, labor, and pensions</strong></span></li>
</ol>
<ul>
<li><strong>Pension adjustment 2027:</strong> For the year 2027, pensions will be increased by 2.95% for monthly pension incomes up to EUR 6,930. For incomes above this threshold, a flat increase of EUR 204.44 will apply.</li>
<li><strong>Maximum contribution base:</strong> The maximum social security contribution base (Höchstbeitragsgrundlage) is specifically adjusted and increased for 2027 and 2028.</li>
<li><strong>Labor market policy:</strong> Employers must continue to pay their share of unemployment insurance contributions for older employees who are no longer personally subject to unemployment insurance, until they reach pension eligibility.</li>
<li><strong>Unemployment benefits:</strong> Stricter measures are introduced for individuals caught working while receiving unemployment benefits without prior notification to the AMS, including a mandatory six-week benefit reclamation.</li>
</ul>
<ol start="3">
<li><strong><span style="text-decoration: underline"> Family and education</span></strong></li>
</ol>
<ul>
<li><strong>Family allowance fund:</strong> Effective 1 January 2028, the Family Allowance Fund will receive an annual allocation of EUR 1.3 billion from income tax revenue. The contribution rate for employers to this fund is set at 2.7% starting in 2028.</li>
<li><strong>University funding:</strong> The Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Finance are tasked with re-evaluating and re-setting the total funding and budget pillars for universities for the 2025–2027 performance agreement period.</li>
</ul>
<ol start="4">
<li><strong><span style="text-decoration: underline"> Environment, climate, and agriculture</span></strong></li>
</ol>
<ul>
<li><strong>Forest and water resilience Act (Wald-Wasser-Resilienzgesetz):</strong> A new law is established to accelerate adaptation to climate change, improve the resilience of forest ecosystems, and enhance the ecological state of water bodies.</li>
<li><strong>Forest resilience fund:</strong> The existing Forest Fund is renamed the “Forest Resilience Fund” (Waldresilienzfonds), with EUR 54 million in federal funds pledged for 2027 and 2028.</li>
<li><strong>Environmental support:</strong> Funding frameworks for environmental measures, including thermal renovation, switching to climate-friendly heating, and industrial transformation, are extended and increased for the period 2027–2031 [168–174].</li>
</ul>
<ol start="5">
<li><span style="text-decoration: underline"><strong> Justice and media</strong></span></li>
</ol>
<ul>
<li><strong>Civil law reform:</strong> The bill abolishes “judicial wills” and the judicial recording of last wills, shifting these functions more exclusively to private or notarial processes.</li>
<li><strong>Court fees:</strong> Various court fees are adjusted, and a new fee is introduced for cases where an appeal is announced but then not actually filed.</li>
<li>ORF reform: The Austrian Broadcasting Corporation (ORF) is required to implement “structural measures” to substantially reduce its cost base in personnel, material costs, and production efficiency to ensure a balanced budget.</li>
</ul>
<ol start="6">
<li><span style="text-decoration: underline"><strong> Infrastructure and mobility</strong></span></li>
</ol>
<ul>
<li><strong>SCHIG renaming:</strong> The Railway Infrastructure Financing Company  is expanded and renamed to “Schieneninfrastruktur-Dienstleistungsgesellschaft mbH”. Its tasks will include the procurement and management of regional bus lines and “Rolling Road” (Rollende Landstraße) freight services.</li>
</ul>

The Department of Finance Canada has published draft legislative proposals to amend the definition of a &#8220;deduction/non-inclusion arrangement&#8221; under subsection 47(1) of the Global Minimum...]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>The Department of Finance Canada has launched a <a href="https://www.canada.ca/en/department-finance/corporate/laws-regulations/draft-legislation/2026/07-gmta-limm.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener">consultation</a> on draft amendments to the Global Minimum Tax Act that would update the definition of a &#8220;deduction/non-inclusion arrangement&#8221; under subsection 47(1).</p>
<p>The Department of Finance Canada has published draft legislative proposals to amend the definition of a &#8220;deduction/non-inclusion arrangement&#8221; under subsection 47(1) of the Global Minimum Tax Act as part of a wider consultation on tax legislation.</p>
<p>The proposals, published on 23 July 2026, would introduce technical changes to the definition used in the Act and are intended to apply to the fiscal years of qualifying Multinational Enterprise (MNE) groups beginning on or after 31 December 2023.</p>
<p><strong>Updated definition proposed</strong></p>
<p>Under the draft legislation, a &#8220;deduction/non-inclusion arrangement&#8221; would mean an arrangement entered into after 15 December 2022 in which one constituent entity of an MNE group provides credit to, or makes an investment in, another constituent entity within the same group.</p>
<p>The arrangement would fall within the definition where it results in an expense or loss in the financial statements of a constituent entity and meets specified conditions relating to revenue recognition and taxable income.</p>
<p><strong>Conditions for qualification</strong></p>
<p>The proposed definition provides that an arrangement would qualify where the expense or loss does not give rise to a commensurate increase in revenue or gain in the financial statements of the constituent entity providing the credit or investment.</p>
<p>In addition, the entity providing the credit or investment must not be reasonably expected to have a commensurate increase in its taxable income over the entire life of the arrangement.</p>
<p><strong>Banking sector exclusion</strong></p>
<p>The draft amendment would continue to exclude expenses or losses that are solely related to qualifying tier one capital issued to satisfy regulatory requirements in the banking sector.</p>
<p><strong>Part of wider legislative package</strong></p>
<p>According to the legislative proposals, the amendment is intended to replace the existing definition in subsection 47(1) of the Global Minimum Tax Act. The package has also been drafted to take into account the potential royal assent of Bill C-31, A second Act to implement certain provisions of the budget tabled in Parliament on 4 November 2025.</p>
<p>If enacted, the revised definition would apply to fiscal years of qualifying MNE groups beginning on or after 31 December 2023.</p>
<p>Stakeholders may submit comments on the consultation until 4 September 2026.</p>

		<category><![CDATA[Europe]]></category>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<p>Portugal approved Modelo 64 tax return form, the official return for the assessment and payment of domestic top-up tax under the Global Minimum Tax Regime (RIMG), following the launch of the Modelo 62 – Registration Declaration form (RIMG) filing service for the 2025 fiscal year. Together, the two forms establish separate procedures for registration and for the assessment and payment of tax under the regime.</p>
<p><strong>Modelo 64 for assessment and payment</strong></p>
<p>Modelo 64 form was approved by <a href="https://diariodarepublica.pt/dr/detalhe/portaria/318-2026-1153221702" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Ordinance No. 318/2026/1</a>, issued by the Secretary of State for Tax Affairs on 17 July 2026 and published on 30 July 2026, as part of Portugal&#8217;s implementation of the OECD Pillar Two framework and the European Union Minimum Tax Directive.</p>
<p>Modelo 64 is used to calculate and settle any top-up tax payable in Portugal by a Constituent Entity or, where applicable, by a Designated Local Entity acting on behalf of a multinational enterprise (MNE) group or a large domestic group.</p>
<p>In general, each Constituent Entity in Portugal must submit the return. Where a Designated Local Entity has been appointed and confirmed, it is responsible for filing on behalf of all Portuguese Constituent Entities and for obtaining the information required to meet the reporting obligations.</p>
<p>The return must be submitted electronically through the Portal das Finanças.</p>
<p>The filing deadline is generally 15 months after the end of the relevant fiscal year. For the first fiscal year in which the regime applies, the deadline is extended to 18 months.</p>
<p>A separate return must be submitted where a Constituent Entity belongs to more than one qualifying group during the same fiscal year. Replacement returns may also be filed to correct factual or legal errors.</p>
<p>There is no filing obligation where no Portuguese top-up tax is payable. In addition, no assessment or collection will be made where the amount of tax assessed is less than EUR 25.</p>
<p><strong>Modelo 62 for registration</strong></p>
<p>The Portuguese Tax and Customs Authority made available the submission service for <a href="https://info.portaldasfinancas.gov.pt/pt/destaques/Paginas/RIMG-Mod62-DeclRegisto.aspx" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Modelo 62</a> –  Registration Declaration form (RIMG) for the 2025 fiscal year – on 3 July 2026.</p>
<p>The declaration is provided for under point (a) of paragraph 1 of Article 45 of the Global Minimum Tax Regime (RIMG), approved by Law No. 41/2024 of 8 November.</p>
<p>Each Constituent Entity in Portugal that belongs to an MNE group within the scope of the regime must submit Modelo 62. A Designated Local Entity may instead submit the declaration on behalf of all Portuguese Constituent Entities in the group.</p>
<p>Where a group becomes subject to the regime during the fiscal year, Modelo 62 must be filed by the last day of the 12th month following the end of that fiscal year. Where there are changes to information previously reported in Modelo 62, the declaration must be filed by the last day of the ninth month following the end of the fiscal year.</p>
<p>Where the first fiscal year in which the group became subject to the RIMG was 2024, a new Modelo 62 for the 2025 fiscal year is required only if there are changes to the information previously declared. In such cases, the complete information relating to the group must be provided.</p>
